verdict.rationale: RustDesk ships its own OSS and Pro rendezvous/relay servers that you deploy on your own infrastructure, so you decide where connection data lives; it markets this as keeping data fully under your control for regulatory compliance. Users report running their own relay servers, though some describe self-hosting as difficult. missing for 10: no region selection or residency guarantees for RustDesk's own public servers, no explicit documentation of what data is stored and where, and mixed hands-on self-hosting reports.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can choose where my data is stored (region/residency)

citations.quote: Regulatory compliance made easy: self-hosted RustDesk keeps your data fully under your control.
Server OSS: a free, open-source ID/rendezvous server (hbbs) and relay server (hbbr) that you can deploy on your own infrastructure.
clients connect peer to peer when they can and fall back to your relay.
You can use our rendezvous/relay server, set up your own, or write your own rendezvous/relay server.
